explanation: Compared against the abstract of arXiv:2110.04263 (Brier, Clavier, Gutsche, Naccache): 'Pick a decimal integer n and multiply all its digits by each other. Repeat the process until a single digit Δ(n) is obtained. [...] The number of steps Ξ(n) needed to reach Δ(n), called the multiplicative persistence of n [...] is conjectured to always be at most 11.' digitProduct is the product of the base-10 digits, with digitProduct 0 = 0 set explicitly (Nat.digits 10 0 = [] would otherwise give 1), so every n < 10 is a fixed point and '∃ k ≤ 11, digitProduct^[k] n < 10' says exactly that the persistence of n is at most 11. Boundary cases: n < 10 holds with k = 0, and a product containing the digit 0 reaches 0. The tests in the file show that 277777788888899 needs exactly 11 steps, so the constant is the conjectured one. Stated as a claim, as in the source. Correct.
